text:
Max Crozier has played 9 of Tampa's games and picked up 3 assists, two of them in a win over the Islanders in October. He played almost 21 minutes in the win over Chicago on Nov. 5, the most he's had in a month, and the Lightning have been winning around him.

His numbers are those of a solid depth defenseman. Tampa takes 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, though the Lightning are slightly better without him. He hasn't scored on 0.86 expected goals. Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level last season, with most of his value on the penalty kill.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, from a small seven-game sample, has one clear weakness: only 18% of his exits keep possession, so he clears it out rather than carrying it. He's 26, a 2019 fourth-round pick from Providence College, with 53 NHL games before this season. We project about 24 points if he plays every night, which he probably won't. He missed Saturday's game in Minnesota. For Tampa, he's insurance, and so far good insurance.
headline: Crozier fills in for Tampa
